extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly; educated general public and scientific practitioners interested in popular scientific news and demonstrations
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or assessing popular-science magazine articles and short reports that describe experiments, technological demonstrations, natural-history observations, and scientific argument for an educated general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illuminating power (photometric output)
rubrics_metrics.description: The machine is capable of giving a light of 12,000 caudle-power, the electric fluid being distributed to four electric lamps, each having the power of three thousand candles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photometric comparison: the light produced was photometrically equal to eight hundred gas-burners, burning five feet of gas per hour each. Use absolute photometric figures (candle-power / gas-burner equivalence) to evaluate performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity and steadiness of illumination
rubrics_metrics.description: The illumination was perfect. The light was very uniform and steady, free from the flickering that used to be an accompaniment of electric light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether lighting is spatially uniform and temporally steady (absence of flicker) during operation and over the areas intended to be illuminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comfort to the eye (softness / endurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering the enormous illuminating power, the light was unexpectedly soft and endurable to the eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure subjective and objective comfort (glare, harshness) despite high luminous output; consider reports of observer comfort and any ocular strain during exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color rendering / whiteness of the light
rubrics_metrics.description: An opportunity was afforded to test the character and whiteness of the light. ... the colors were brought out as clearly as by the full light of the sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ability of the light source to render colors faithfully (visual tests with colored fabrics or objective color-rendering metrics) compared to sunlight or established standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational cost and economic efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The total cost of the whole light from the four lamps, including the items of consumption of carbon in the lamps, interest on the investment, and wear and tear, would not exceed thirty cents per hour. ... This amount of gas would cost eight dollars per hour in Cleveland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute per-hour operational cost including consumables, capital amortization, maintenance, and compare to alternatives (e.g., gas) when assessing viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and practical installation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: The electric fluid being distributed to four electric lamps, two of the lamps were placed on the third and two on the fourth floor of the immense building. The illumination ... streamed out at all the windows, illuminating houses and streets for a long distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how power is distributed to multiple fixtures/floors, installation practicality, and effective reach of illumination in real building layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical antiseptic application for contagion prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Topical application of substances inimical to the development of contagia: charging the mouth and nostrils with antiseptic substances so as to render the breath and the tissues ... unfriendly to the development of the contagium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a disease shows marked local manifestations (e.g., diphtheria, scarlet fever), topical antiseptics to portals of entry are indicated; evaluate agent's local effectiveness, safety, and application practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic introduction of antiseptic/antifermentative agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction into the blood of substances which shall prevent fermentive, defibrinizing or destructive processes. ... the fluids, glands, etc., of the system are so permeated with the antiseptic or antifementative agent as to be able to withstand the action of the disease-germ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider systemic administration to create constitutional resistance: verify that agents reach secretions/blood (evidence such as chlorate of potassium found in secretions, hematological changes after dosing) and weigh systemic risks vs benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match intervention to disease presentation (local vs constitutional)
rubrics_metrics.description: In diseases like diphtheria and scarlet fever, which at the outset have such marked local manifestation ... topical application of remedies seems to be clearly indicated. But ... the introduction of certain substances into the blood is a still more effectual mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide between topical and systemic approaches based on disease's pathophysiology and stage; use local measures when disease is primarily local, systemic agents when constitutional protection is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity and durability of creosote-treated timber
rubrics_metrics.description: Railway-ties, dried, and saturated with creosote, will last ... for twenty years or more in good condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate treated timber by expected service life; check that spikes do not corrode or work loose and that surfaces under rails resist decay and wear under alternating wet/dry conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to marine borers and suitability for submerged use
rubrics_metrics.description: Creosoted timber is proof against the ravages of the Teredo navalis and other mollusks which cause such destruction of timbers submerged in sea-water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For wharf and ship-building use, assess treated timber's resistance to marine borers through exposure tests or historical performance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of wood species for creosoting (absorption characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The woods best adapted for the creosoting process are those which are light and porous, as these most readily absorb the creosote; ... White pine absorbs creosote like a sponge, and the yellow pine of the South takes it readily also. ... spruce is a firm, compact wood, and absorbs oil with more difficulty; neither does it require so much to preserve it. Oak has a coarse fibre, and is easily treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select wood species based on porosity and oil-absorption characteristics; lighter, more porous woods absorb preservative more readily and may be made durable and cost-effective alternatives to costly timbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and stability of observable experimental configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: Three magnetized needles in cork floats arrange themselves at the vertices of an equilateral triangle; raise and lower the magnet and the needles change separation, and with more needles characteristic arrangements appear (figures obtained up to twenty needles). Some observed arrangements are not stable when the magnet is raised and replaced quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess experiments by their reproducibility, stability of resulting configurations, and sensitivity to perturbations (e.g., how quickly changing the external field returns system to stable or unstable states). Note whether procedures produce repeatable 'figures' and whether variations produce systematic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory must explain observed discrepancies and propose plausible mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for Mars's inner satellite moving with a relative velocity much higher than the axial rotation of Mars, Prof. Doolittle proposes three ways interstellar matter (meteorites) might have modified relative velocities: (1) impacts on the satellite forcing it into a narrower orbit; (2) impacts on the primary increasing its mass and attraction; (3) increasing the primary's mass and reducing its absolute velocity, thereby increasing the satellite's relative velocity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a theoretical discrepancy appears (observational vs expected), require the theory to offer concrete mechanisms (ideally testable or consistent with known physics) that could produce the observed effect; enumerate and evaluate alternate mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental demonstration of suspended embryonic life (suspended animation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An egg left at ordinary temperature for two or three days after three days under a hen, then again placed under incubation, hatched normally; shows life may be suspended for a considerable length of time in warm-blooded animals without fatal effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled experiments showing reversible suspension of embryonic development; reproducibility, controls (timing, temperatures), and subsequent normal development are evidence for suspended animation claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for extreme structural variation in organisms under identical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Crustaceans and fishes taken from depths of 1,500 to 1,900 fathoms present diametrically opposite conditions with respect to vision — some eyeless, others with enormously developed eyes — differences explained by 'survival of the fittest' under evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In explaining biological variation at similar environmental conditions, consider evolutionary explanations (selection/obliteration) and document structural modifications that substitute for or accompany organ reduction or enlargement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for inductive (empirical) method over speculative a priori reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of technico-inductive science is named because its results are due to the fact that in natural science speculation has given way to induction, the method which is 'nothing else but common-sense applied to a given problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scientific claims and historical interpretations by their grounding in inductive investigation and reproducible empirical evidence rather than speculative a priori reasoning; prize reproducible experimentation and observation as the route to reliable knowledge.
